findings.title: No double-check after acquiring the write lock: duplicate loads and a valid cache can be clobbered with nil
findings.body:
`GetWebAssets` reads the cache under `RLock`, releases it, and then takes the write lock without re-checking whether another goroutine has already populated `entryPointAssetsCache` in the meantime. Two consequences on a cold start where many requests arrive concurrently (the common case, e.g. several browser tabs hitting the index page):

1. Every goroutine that observed `ret == nil` re-runs the full manifest load (disk read / JSON decode, and the CDN HTTP fetch if `cdn` is ever non-empty), serialized one after another behind the exclusive lock, instead of just reusing the value the first goroutine stored.
2. More importantly, line 69 unconditionally assigns `entryPointAssetsCache = result`. If a later goroutine's reload fails (file transiently unreadable, truncated manifest during a rebuild, CDN error), `result` is nil and the already-published, valid cache is overwritten with nil, so subsequent callers fall back to re-reading from disk again.

Fix by re-checking `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` right after acquiring the write lock, and by only assigning to the cache when `err == nil`/`result != nil`.

findings.title: Exclusive lock is held across blocking I/O (file read and CDN HTTP request)
findings.body: The write lock acquired at line 48 is held (via `defer`) for the whole duration of `readWebAssetsFromCDN` (an HTTP request whose only bound is the request context) and `readWebAssetsFromFile` (open + JSON decode). All other callers of `GetWebAssets` block on the mutex during that time. In `setting.Dev` mode the early return is skipped, so *every* index-page request takes the exclusive lock and does a disk read + JSON decode while holding it, fully serializing page loads. Consider loading outside the lock (or using `sync.Once`/`singleflight`) and only taking the lock for the pointer assignment.
